verses.sanskrit:
सञ्जय उवाच।
              पुत्रस्तु ते महाराज रथस्थो रथिनां वरः। दुरुत्सहो बभौ युद्धे यथा रुद्रः प्रतापवान्॥१॥
तस्य बाणसहस्रैस्तु प्रच्छन्ना ह्यभवन्मही। परांश्च सिषिचे बाणैर्धाराभिरिव पर्वतान्॥२॥
verses.english: With the thousands of arrows shot by him, the Earth was completely covered. He drenched his enemies with showers of arrows like the clouds pouring rain on mountain breasts.

verses.sanskrit: न च सोऽस्ति पुमान्कश्चित्पाण्डवानां बलार्णवे। हयो गजो रथो वापि यः स्याद्बाणैरविक्षतः॥३॥
यं यं हि समरे योधं प्रपश्यामि विशाम्पते। स स बाणैश्चितोऽभूद्वै पुत्रेण तव भारत॥४॥
verses.english: O king, amongst the warriors every one, O Bharata, was struck by your son with his arrows.

verses.sanskrit: यथा सैन्येन रजसा समुद्भूतेन वाहिनी। प्रत्यदृश्यत सञ्छन्ना तथा बाणैर्महात्मनः॥५॥
बाणभूतामपश्याम पृथिवीं पृथिवीपते। दुर्योधनेन प्रकृतां क्षिप्रहस्तेन धन्विना॥६॥
verses.english: The Earth then, O king, was as if converted into one sheet of arrows by your son Duryodhana, that bowman endued with great lightness of hand.

verses.sanskrit: तेषु योधसहस्रेषु तावकेषु परेषु च। एको दुर्योधनो ह्यासीत्पुमानिति मतिर्मम॥७॥
verses.english: Amongst those thousands of warriors on the field, of your side or that of the enemy, it appeared as if Duryodhana was then the only man.

verses.sanskrit: तत्राद्भुतमपश्याम तव पुत्रस्य विक्रमम्। यदेकं सहिताः पार्था नाभ्यवर्तन्त भारत॥८॥
verses.english: The prowess displayed by your son was highly wonderful, since the Parthas, even in a body, could not approach him who was single.

verses.sanskrit: युधिष्ठिरं शतेनाजौ विव्याध भरतर्षभ। भीमसेनं च सप्तत्या सहदेवं च पञ्चभिः॥९॥
नकुलं त चतुःषष्ट्या धृष्टद्युम्नं च पञ्चभिः। सप्तभिर्द्रौपदेयांश्च त्रिभिर्विव्याध सात्यकिम्॥१०॥
verses.english: And he struck Nakula with sixty four and Dhrishtadyumna with five and the sons of Draupadi with seven and Satyaki with three arrows. With a broad-headed arrow, he then, O king, cut off the bow of Sahadeva.

verses.sanskrit: धनुश्चिच्छेद भल्लेन सहदेवस्य मारिष। तदपास्य धनुश्छिन्नं माद्रीपुत्रः प्रतापवान्॥११॥
अभ्यद्रवत राजानं प्रगृह्यान्यन्महद्धनुः। ततो दुर्योधनं सङ्ख्ये विव्याध दशभिः शरैः॥१२॥
नकुलस्तु ततो वीरो राजानं नवभिः शरैः। घोररूपैर्महेष्वासो विव्याध च ननाद च॥१३॥
verses.english: The great and brave bowman Nakula then struck the king with nine terrible arrows and uttered a loud war cry.

verses.sanskrit: सात्यकिश्चैव राजानं शरेणानतपर्वणा। द्रौपदेयास्त्रिसप्तत्या धर्मराजश्च पञ्चभिः॥१४॥
verses.english: Satyaki struck the king with a single straight shaft; the sons of Draupadi struck him with seventy three and king Yudhishthira struck him with five. And Bhimasena assailed the king with eighty arrows.

verses.sanskrit: अशीत्या भीमसेनश्च शरै राजानमार्पयन्। समन्तात्कीर्यमाणस्तु बाणसङ्धैर्महात्मभिः॥१५॥
न चचाल महाराज सर्वसैन्यस्य पश्यतः। लाघवं सौष्ठवं चापि वीर्यं चापि महात्मनः॥१६॥
verses.english: Though struck thus from all sides with numerous arrows by those illustrious warriors, Duryodhana still, O king, did not waver, in the presence of all the soldiers assembled there.

verses.sanskrit: अतिसर्वाणि भूतानि ददृशुः सर्वमानवाः। धार्तराष्ट्रा हि राजेन्द्र योधास्तु स्वल्पमन्तरम्॥१७॥
verses.english: The quickness, the skill and the prowess of that illustrious warrior excelled those of every man.

verses.sanskrit: अपश्यमाना राजानं पर्यवर्तन्त दंशिताः। तेषामापततां घोरस्तुमुलः समपद्यत॥१८॥
verses.english: Meanwhile the Dhartarashtras, O king, who had not fled far away, beholding the king, rallied and returned there, clad in mail.

verses.sanskrit: क्षुब्धस्य हि समुद्रस्य प्रावृट्काले यथा स्वनः। समासाद्य रणे ते तु राजानमपराजितम्॥१९॥
verses.english: The noise made by them when they returned was exceedingly awful, like the roar of the surging deep during the rainy season.

verses.sanskrit: प्रत्युद्ययुर्महेष्वासाः पाण्डवानाततायिनः। भीमसेनं रणे क्रुद्धो द्रोणपुत्रो न्यवारयत्॥२०॥
verses.english: The son of Drona opposed in that battle the angry Bhimasena.

verses.sanskrit: नानाबाणैर्महाराज प्रमुक्तैः सर्वतोदिशम्। नाज्ञायन्त रणे वीरा न दिशः प्रदिशः कुतः॥२१॥
verses.english: With the arrows, O king, that were shot in that battle, all the points of the horizon were completely covered, so that the brave warriors could not distinguish the cardinal from the subsidiary points of the compass.

verses.sanskrit: तावुभौ क्रूरकर्माणावुभौ भारत दुःसहौ। घोररूपमयुध्येतां कृतप्रतिकृतैषिणौ॥२२॥
verses.english: As regards Ashvatthaman and Bhimasena, O Bharata, both of them performed wonderful feats. Both of them were invincible in battle. The arms of both continued marks of bowstring for having repeatedly drawn the same. Opposing each other, they fought on, frightening the entire universe.

verses.sanskrit: त्रासयन्तौ दिशः सर्वा ज्याक्षेपकठिनत्वचौ। शकुनिस्तु रणे वीरो युधिष्ठिरमपीडयत्॥२३॥
तस्याश्वांश्चतुरो हत्वा सुबलस्य सुतो विभो। नादं चकार बलवत्सर्वसैन्यानि कोपयन्॥२४॥
verses.english: The heroic Shakuni struck Yudhishthira in that battle. Having killed the four horses of the king the powerful son of Subala uttered a loud roar, making all the soldiers tremble with fear.

verses.sanskrit: एतस्मिन्नन्तरे वीरं राजानमपराजितम्। अपोवाह रथेनाजौ सहदेवः प्रतापवान्॥२५॥
verses.english: Meanwhile the valiant Şahadeva carried away the heroic but defeated king on his car from that battle.

verses.sanskrit: अथान्यं रथमास्थाय धर्मपुत्रो युधिष्ठिरः। शकुनिं नरभिर्विद्ध्वा पुनर्विव्याध पञ्चभिः॥२६॥
verses.english: Then riding on another car, returned king Yudhishthira and having pierced Shakuni at first with nine arrows, once more struck him with five. And that best of all bowmen then sent up a loud roar.

verses.sanskrit: ननाद च महानादं प्रवरः सर्वधन्विनाम्। तद्युद्धमभवच्चित्रं घोररूपं च मारिष॥२७॥
verses.english: That battle presented a wonderful spectacle, It filled the spectators with delight and was praised by the Siddhas and the Charanas.

verses.sanskrit: प्रेक्षतां प्रीतिजननं सिद्धचारणसेवितम्। उलूकस्तु महेष्वासं नकुलं युद्धदुर्मदम्॥२८॥
अभ्यद्रवदमेयात्मा शरवर्षैः समन्ततः। तथैव नकुलः शूरः सौबलस्य सुतं रणे॥२९॥
verses.english: Heroic Uluka rushed against the mighty bowman Nakula, in that battle, discharging showers of arrows from all sides.

verses.sanskrit: शरवर्षेण महता समन्तात्पर्यवारयत्। तौ तत्र समरे वीरो कुलपुत्रौ महारथौ॥३०॥
verses.english: The heroic Nakula, however, in that battle opposed the son of Shakuni with a dense shower of arrows from every side.

verses.sanskrit: योधयन्तावपश्येतां कृतप्रतिकृतैषिणौ। तथैव कृतवर्माणं शैनेयः शत्रुतापनः॥३१॥
verses.english: Both those heroes were born in high family and both were great car-warriors. They were seen to fight with each other, each enraged with the other.

verses.sanskrit: योधयञ्शुशुभे राजन्बलिं शक्र इवाहवे। दुर्योधनो धनुश्छित्त्वा धृष्टद्युम्नस्य संयुगे॥३२॥
verses.english: Similarly Kritavarman, O king, fighting with the grandson of Shini, that scorcher of foes, shone like Shakra fighting with the Asura Vala.

verses.sanskrit: अथैनं छिन्नधन्वानं विव्याध निशितैः शरैः। धृष्टद्युम्नोऽपि समरे प्रगृह्य परमायुधम्॥३३॥
verses.english: Having cut off Dhrishtadyumna's bow in that battle, Dhrishtadyumna struck his bowless antagonist with kcen arrows.

verses.sanskrit: राजानं योधयामास पश्यतां सर्वधन्विनाम्। तयोर्युद्धं महच्चासीत्सङ्ग्रामे भरतर्षभ॥३४॥
verses.english: Then, in that battle, having taken up a formidable bow, Dhrishtadyumna fought with the king before all the bowmen.

verses.sanskrit: प्रभिन्नयोर्यथासक्तं मत्तयोर्वरहस्तिनोः। गौतमस्तु रणे क्रुद्धो द्रौपदेयान्महाबलान्॥३५॥
verses.english: The encounter between those two heroes was exceedingly dreadful, O best of Bharata's race, like that between two wild and infuriate elephants with temporal juice trickling down.

verses.sanskrit: विव्याध बहुभिः शूरः शरैः सन्नतपर्वभिः। तस्य तैरभवद्युद्धमिन्द्रियैरिव देहिनः॥३६॥
verses.english: Worked up with rage in that battle, the heroic Gautama struck the mighty sons of Draupadi with many straight arrows.

verses.sanskrit: घोररूपमसंवार्यं निर्मर्यादमवर्तत। ते च सम्पीडयामासुरिन्द्रियाणीव बालिशम्॥३७॥
verses.english: The encounter that took place between him and those five resembled that which takes place between a man and his five senses. It was awful and fierce and no party showed any consideration for the other.

verses.sanskrit: स च तान्प्रति संरब्धः प्रत्ययोधयदाहवे। एवं चित्रमभूद्युद्धं तस्य तैः सह भारत॥३८॥
verses.english: The five sons of Draupadi assailed Kripa like the senses afflicting a foolish man. He, on the other hand, fighting with thein, opposed them vigorously.

verses.sanskrit: उत्थायोत्थाय हि यथा देहिनामिन्द्रयैर्विभो। नराश्चैव नरैः सार्धं दन्तिनो दन्तिभिस्तथा॥३९॥
verses.english: That battle between him and them was indeed wonderful because it resembled the struggles, O king, between men and their Senses.

verses.sanskrit: हया हयैः समासक्ता रथिनो राथभिः सह। सङ्कुलं चाभवद्भूयो घोररूपं विशाम्पते॥४०॥
verses.english: Men fought with men, elephants with elephants, horses with horses and car-warriors with car-warriors. Once more O king, that encounter became general and dreadful.

verses.sanskrit: इदं चित्रमिदं घोरमिदं रौद्रमिति प्रभो। युद्धान्यासन्महाराज घोराणि च बहूनि च॥४१॥
verses.english: Here an encounter was beautiful, there another was dicadful and there another was exceedingly fierce. O lord, many dreadful encounters took place in course of that battle.

verses.sanskrit: ते समासाद्य समरे परस्परमरिन्दमाः। व्यनदंश्चैव जघ्नुश्च समासाद्य महाहवे॥४२॥
verses.english: Belonging to both armies and encountering one another, those chastisers of foes struck and killed one another in that dreadful battle.

verses.sanskrit: तेषां पत्रसमुद्भूतं रजस्तीव्रमदृश्यत। वातेन चोद्धतं राजन्धावद्भिश्चाश्वसादिभिः॥४३॥
verses.english: A thick cloud of dust was raised by the cars and the animals. Thick dust was also raised by the running of the horses, a dust that was carried from one place to another by the wind.

verses.sanskrit: रथनेमिसमुद्भूतं निःश्वासैश्चापि दन्तिनाम्। रजःसन्ध्याभ्रकलिलं दिवाकरपथं ययौ॥४४॥
verses.english: A dust, thick as an evening cloud, was caused in the sky by the wheels of cars and the breaths of the elephants.

verses.sanskrit: रजसा तेन सम्पृक्तो भास्करो निष्प्रभः कृतः। सञ्छादिताऽभवद्भूमिस्ते च शूरा महारथाः॥४५॥
verses.english: On that dust being raised and the sun himself hidden therewith, the Earth became shrouded and the heroic and great car-warriors were not visible.

verses.sanskrit: मुहूर्तादिव संवृत्तं नीरजस्कं समन्ततः। वीरशोणितसिक्तायां भूमौ भरतसत्तम॥४६॥
verses.english: That dust disappeared and everything became clear when the Earth, O best of the Bharatas, was covered with the blood of heroes.

verses.sanskrit: उपाशाम्यत्ततस्तीव्रं तद्रजो घोरदर्शनम्। ततोऽपश्यमहं भूयो द्वन्द्वयुद्धानि भारत॥४७॥
verses.english: When that dense and awful cloud of dust was put down there were seen many single encounters, O Bharata, that the heroes fought at the noon each according to his strength and his rank. They were all exceedingly fierce. The sheen of the weapons in those encounters, O king, appeared full in view.

verses.sanskrit: यथाप्राणं यथाश्रेष्ठं मध्याह्ने वै सुदारुणे। वर्मणां तत्र राजेन्द्र व्यदृश्यन्तोज्ज्वला प्रभाः॥४८॥
शब्दश्च तुमुलः सङ्ख्ये शराणां पततामभूत्। महावेणुवनस्येव दह्यमानस्य पर्वते॥४९॥
